s001.text: UPSC, twenty twenty-three. General Studies Paper One, ten marks, one hundred and fifty words. Why is the South-West Monsoon called Purvaiya, easterly, in the Bhojpur region? And how has this wind system influenced the region's culture? Here's the puzzle. A south-west monsoon with an east wind's name.

s002.text: Read what it asks. Why asks for a cause. How has it influenced asks for effects. So there are two jobs. The reason for the name. And the mark it left on culture.

s003.text: Start with the word. In Bhojpuri song, purva is the easterly wind. A song collected in Jaunpur reads, gusts of easterly winds blow.

s004.text: But the monsoon is south-west. Yes, over the sea. Then the Bay of Bengal branch meets the Arakan Hills. It bends, and runs west up the Ganga plain. So it arrives from the east.

s005.text: IMD gives the weather map. Its monsoon trough runs from Ganganagar through Prayagraj to Kolkata. North of that line, winds are easterly or south-easterly. Placing Bhojpur there is our own step. IMD never names it, so say it with care.

s006.text: Now the culture. The rains set the farm calendar. Paddy sowing runs from the third week of June to the fourth week of July. A Jaunpur work song says, it's raining, let's go transplant paddy.

s007.text: Now we write. One hundred and fifty words, about seven minutes. Open by translating the word. Purva means easterly. Then the Bay branch.

s008.text: Section one is the cause. The Bay branch turns west. The trough has easterlies on its north. Then say plainly that placing Bhojpur there is our inference. Add a small flow diagram.

s009.text: Section two is the culture. Farming first, with the paddy dates. Then Kajari, sung by women in Sawan, July and August. That slack season lets wives visit their parents. And fifty million people speak Bhojpuri.

s010.text: Last, the ache. Migration shaped Biraha, Bidesiya and Kajari. The same wind that should comfort pains a wife whose husband is away. Rain is a boon for the fields and a pain for the parted. End on that.

s011.text: Now the easy answer beside it. It invents an origin for the word, from a suffix. It says a south-west monsoon cannot be easterly. It credits festivals to the wind with no source. It says the wind only brings joy. And it says IMD named the Bhojpur wind. It did not.

s012.text: Here is the payoff. The same frame answers its cousins. Twenty twenty-two asked about the cloudburst. Twenty nineteen asked why the monsoon is erratic. Learn it once: the cause first, then its effects.
